messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after last kernel-selector rollout (deployed ~2143620000) we're seeing a p90 latency regression on paged-attn paths for seq~512 :thinking:

sam: saw the dashboard spike too. do you have numbers?

maria: pre-roll p90 seq512 = 82ms, post-roll p90 = 137ms, p99 up to ~420ms. throughput looks fine, error rates unchanged. seems isolated to paged-flash variants.

jen: can you paste the profiler stack / top kernels? even a tiny flame snippet helps.

maria: pasted sampling from perf-runner (seq512, batch=4, kv warm):
```
Top kernels: flash_paged_attn_kernel_v2  48%
kv_prefetch_copy                           18%
softmax_fused                              12%
memcpy_h2d                                 9%
other                                       13%
```
looks like selector is choosing flash_paged_attn_kernel_v2 more often. v2 has path that triggers extra memcpy for certain stride shapes.

alex: that matches a change in the selector landed in commit 3a9f6b (prefer v2 for seq>=256). previous rule favored v1 for cached-KV-heavy workloads.

sam: could be interaction with KV cold vs warm. any difference if cache hot?

maria: good call — I ran a warmup test (100 inferences before measuring):
- cold p90=137ms
- warm p90=92ms
so warming drops a lot but still ~10ms above baseline. p99 tails still show spikes.

jen: so two effects: (1) selector picks v2 causing memcpy overhead on certain stride shapes, (2) KV warmup hides some but not all. we should confirm by forcing kernel.

maria: test: force legacy kernel with env var:
```bash
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy_prefer_v1
./bench --model gpt-xx --seq 512 --batch 4
```
result: p90=84ms, p99 ~170ms. back near baseline.

alex: strong signal then. propose bisecting selector change and also measure batching heuristic influence. the selector change landed with batching tweak in same PR.

perf-bot: CI bench link: https://ci.internal/bench/2143/paged-attn/compare/3a9f6b..HEAD :eyes:

sam: quick micro-experiment — override batching heuristic to smaller micro-batches (force batch_split=2) and run with v2:
```json
{"batch_split":2}
```
result: p90 drops from 137ms -> 101ms. seems batch splitting masks memcpy cost.

jen: so batching heuristics and selector interact. plan: (A) bisect selector commits to isolate the exact line, (B) run variant with v2 but force smaller batch splits as a temporary mitigation, (C) test canary rollback of selector rule for dedicated pool.

maria: bisect started: narrowing to commit range 3a9f6b..3a9f6f. running nightly bisect bench now (ETA ~30m).

alex: also check kernel build flags — the memcpy path in v2 is guarded by ENABLE_STRIDE_COPY. if we can guard it behind a kv-warm check maybe avoid extra copy when KV cache is present.

sam: noted. I'll try a runtime patch: avoid stride-copy when kv_popcount > threshold. quick patch locally, small test: p90=89ms, p99 reduced.

maria: good. for immediate mitigation I'm going to flip the selector in canary (dedicated-c1) to prefer v1 for seq>=384 and monitor. will post canary link.

perf-bot: Canary started: https://canary.internal/dedicated-c1/2143654321-monitor :party_parrot:

jen: follow-ups: add a unit micro-benchmark that exercises the stride shape and KV warm/cold modes, add regression alert for seq512 p90 > 110ms, and add a note in release changelog about selector change.

maria: assigning follow-ups: sam owns runtime patch PR, jen owns micro-bench & alert, alex owns selector bisect/rollback plan. I'll watch the canary and roll back if p90 > 120ms after 1h.

alex: thumbs up. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: one more: save profiler traces to s3 under /perf/traces/2143654321 for postmortem.

sam: uploading now. done. link: s3://redwood-perf/perf-traces/2143654321/trace.tar.gz

maria: closing the thread for now, will reopen if canary regresses. thanks! :eyes:
